citation: Mertel, K. (2020). Heidegger, Technology and Education. Journal of Philosophy of Education, 54(2), 467-486.
discipline: Continental philosophy of technology / philosophy of education
thesis: Situates Heidegger's account of technology as Gestell (enframing) within the emancipatory project of early fundamental ontology (Being and Time), emphasizing language and self-appropriation, in order to defend it against charges of fatalism/dystopianism and to argue that a positive Heideggerian programme of education should center 'moral articulacy' and multilingualism rather than the 'skilled bodily coping' model defended by Dreyfus and Wrathall.
boredom_engagement: NONE DIRECT — zero occurrences of 'bored/boredom/tedium/ennui/monoton-' in the full extracted text; entry retained for its Gestell/education and Leistungskultur (achievement-culture) argument, linked to Part III only by analogy.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.summary: Technology as Gestell/enframing; reality disclosed as homogeneous 'standing reserve' (Bestand); calculative thinking as the corresponding mode of access.

sections.heading: Fundamental Ontology as an Emancipatory Project
sections.summary: Dasein's self-alienation as reification; hermeneutics of facticity as de-alienation project; formal indicators as non-reifying language; appropriation as Dasein's fundamental hermeneutical relation; 'ownedness'/'unownedness' preferred over 'authenticity'/'inauthenticity'.

sections.heading: Language and Appropriation in Fundamental Ontology
sections.summary: Language as 'taming of the overwhelming'; appropriation tied to mineness (Jemeinigkeit); education as collaborative co-appropriation vs. fixed 'learning outcomes'.

sections.heading: Situating Enframing Within Fundamental Ontology
sections.summary: Against Marcuse/Feenberg's reading of enframing as static transcendental structure; enframing as historically inherited, revisable horizon; education's task to make Being 'matter'; de-worlding reduces students to system-function (via Crowell, Thomson).

sections.heading: Education as Response to Enframing
sections.summary: Critique of vague Technologically Enhanced Learning (TEL) initiatives (Bayne 2014); Gelassenheit/Besinnung as corrective to calculative thinking.

sections.heading: Thinking as Gelassenheit and Besinnung
sections.summary: Workspace example distinguishing functional vs. eudaimonic vocabulary; schools as 'worlds of significance'; language's world-disclosing function (Gadamer); multilingual dialogue with Japanese interlocutor as model.

sections.heading: The Limits of the Skilled Coping Model
sections.summary: Critiques Dreyfus/Wrathall's sport-as-non-optionalised-engagement example as colonized by economic imperatives; introduces Leistungskultur (achievement culture), burnout, and student anxiety; critiques Feenberg's optimistic reading of social media as Heideggerian 'saying'.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.summary: Appropriative approach (moral articulacy + multilingualism) better founds emancipatory education than the pragmatist/skilled-coping alternative.

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.note: Mertel's own vocabulary is 'de-worlding' and 'homogenisation of life and learning paths' / 'impossible quantification of the qualitative' (via Thomson); never framed as monotony or meaninglessness by the source itself.

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.note: Via Dreyfus/Wrathall's sport-as-'non-optionalised engagement' example, discussed critically by Mertel; term 'flow' never used by source.

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.note: Via the calculative-thinking (mindless/automatic) vs. Gelassenheit/Besinnung (patient/reflective) contrast; attentional vocabulary never used by source.

readings.claim: Heidegger's philosophy of technology continues, rather than abandons, the emancipatory aims of fundamental ontology; the early/late discontinuity thesis wrongly insulates the technology critique from its ethical roots.
Formal indicators and appropriation give fundamental ontology an ineliminably ontic, revisable dimension; enframing is an inherited, not fully closed, horizon of intelligibility.
Education is properly a collaborative process of co-appropriation oriented toward students 'coming into their own,' not toward standardized learning outcomes.
Enframing's de-worlding tendency individualizes what are actually social/systemic pathologies in education, locating the problem in the student rather than the environment.

The pragmatist skilled-bodily-coping model of Heideggerian education (Dreyfus, Wrathall) cannot by itself resist enframing because its paradigm cases (professional/academy sport) are already colonized by economic imperatives, and because it neglects language.

The 'culture of achievement' (Leistungskultur) is an under-discussed by-product of enframing in education, linked (via cited literature) to burnout and rising student anxiety from pre-kindergarten onward.
The proper response to enframing is cultivating 'moral articulacy' via a non-instrumental, multilingual education.
Feenberg's optimistic reading of online platforms as sites of authentic Heideggerian 'saying' mistakes quantity of communication for quality.

interlocutors.name: Andrew Feenberg
interlocutors.role: contested — 'dystopian/fatalistic' charge against Heidegger; optimistic reading of social-media 'saying' contested

interlocutors.name: Hubert Dreyfus
interlocutors.role: contested — skilled bodily coping model of Heideggerian education

interlocutors.name: Mark Wrathall
interlocutors.role: contested (partially endorsed) — skilled coping / sport-as-non-optionalised-engagement; Gelassenheit gloss endorsed

interlocutors.name: Herbert Marcuse
interlocutors.role: contested — static/transcendental reading of enframing rejected

interlocutors.name: Iain Thomson
interlocutors.role: cited approvingly — quantification of the qualitative; importance of education for resisting enframing (2019 piece, not the 2001 'Ontological Education' essay)

interlocutors.name: Steven Crowell
interlocutors.role: cited approvingly — 'things are indifferently valid' / counter-word (Gegen-wort)

interlocutors.name: Siân Bayne
interlocutors.role: cited — critique of Technologically Enhanced Learning (TEL) initiatives

interlocutors.name: Hans-Georg Gadamer
interlocutors.role: cited approvingly — 'to possess a language is to possess a world'
